title: Lena and the Autopsy
premise: When estate lawyer Freya Villalobos is handed a will naming a dead man as beneficiary, she discovers the town founder's coffin exhumed for a property dispute is empty. Teaming up with Lena, the founder's estranged granddaughter and the only heir the will protects, Freya uncovers a decades-old cover-up: the founder faked his death to escape blackmail, and someone has been killing the witnesses ever since. As the killer closes in on Lena, Freya stages a fake exhumation of her own, luring the killer into the crypt where the founder's body — hidden in plain sight for forty years — finally surfaces, and the truth of who protected him all along is the case's cruelest twist.
about_author: Paloma Fairweather is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years in a small-town records office, where she learned that every filing cabinet hides a body. She writes mysteries from a converted funeral parlor on the coast, where the neighbors still don't know.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She reads a will dated three days after the founder Edmund Hale's death, naming a beneficiary who cannot legally exist. The paper is authentic; the signature is Edmund's own. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Empty Oak, Empty Grave
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The county exhumes Hale for a boundary lawsuit and the coffin holds only river stones and a 1979 newspaper. Freya recognizes the stones' arrangement as deliberate — a message. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Lena
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, arriving in town for the funeral of her grandmother. She learns the exhumation happened and that her name appears in the impossible will. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by a door she thought was closed forever opening.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She revisits the three deaths she privately solved — a boater, a faller, a sleeper — and realizes all three notarized documents for Hale's estate. Emotional beat: cold recognition that her old cases were one case.

chapters.title: The Records Room at Midnight
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She breaks into the county annex and finds her grandmother's name signed as a witness on Hale's death certificate — dated a year after his burial. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with hope.

chapters.title: A Lawyer's Confession
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, telling Lena over cold coffee how she solved the three accidents and what it cost her — a partnership dissolved, a reputation for seeing corpses in paperwork. Emotional beat: two guarded people choosing to trust.

chapters.title: The Blackmail Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In Hale's sealed safety deposit box: a ledger of payments from six townspeople, dated across forty years. Four payers are dead. Emotional beat: the town's beloved history cracking like old plaster.

chapters.title: What the Stones Said
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She decodes the river stones as a map to the flooded quarry, and finds a fresh dive line someone else left last week. Emotional beat: the race has already started and they're behind.

chapters.title: The Second Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Someone files paperwork to exhume Hale's wife's coffin, forcing Freya to stall a judge while realizing her own name is now on the killer's list. Emotional beat: the investigator becomes the evidence.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Payers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She attends the historical society dinner and interviews the two living ledger names — the retired sheriff and the florist — watching their faces when Hale's name is toasted. Emotional beat: menace hiding under casseroles and small talk.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Alibi
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The old sheriff confesses to taking hush money but produces proof he was hospitalized during the third 'accident' — meaning a sixth payer exists, one who never signed. Emotional beat: the map has a blank space shaped like a person.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Diving the quarry, she finds a rusted strongbox and a modern air tank — someone has been visiting the site recently. She is watched from the ridge. Emotional beat: terror surfacing with her.

chapters.title: The Case File Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The killer mails her pages of her own private notes on the three accidents, annotated in red. He knows her methods better than she does. Emotional beat: violation; the hunt inverts.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Among her grandmother's effects, letters reveal the wife knew Hale was alive and helped hide him — and that Lena's mother's death was the price of silence. Emotional beat: inherited grief becomes inherited purpose.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She files for a public exhumation of the wife's coffin, announcing it in the paper — bait. Lena objects; they fight about using family grief as a lure. Emotional beat: found family strained by the cost of the plan.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, keeping vigil in the cemetery. She sees the florist's van, then loses sight of him, then finds her car's brake line cut. Emotional beat: the killer is closer than the plan allowed.

chapters.title: The Crypt
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The killer — the county records clerk, the silent sixth name, Hale's illegitimate son — corners Freya in the crypt, confessing he killed to inherit the secret that made his father a ghost. Emotional beat: the banality of the monster.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Held
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The wife's coffin is opened before the town: inside, Edmund Hale's actual remains, hidden by his wife forty years ago. The empty grave was her final message. Emotional beat: a dead woman's posthumous testimony.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The killer, exposed by his own obsession with the case file, is taken alive — but only after nearly sealing Freya in the crypt. The sheriff's old shame helps convict him. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Reading the Real Will
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The impossible will is validated: Hale left everything to Lena and a trust for the town's forgotten — the found family he never claimed in life. Emotional beat: inheritance as apology.

chapters.title: The Quarry Drains
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The town drains the quarry and finds the strongbox's twin: Hale's confession of the original crime he fled. Freya chooses what to publish and what to bury. Emotional beat: mercy as an editorial decision.

chapters.title: Headstones
chapters.summary: Lena and Freya's alternating POV, closing scene. Two new stones by the river: one for Hale under his true name, one for the grandmother who kept him. Lena stays in town. Emotional beat: memory, tended like a garden, becomes home.
